newsitem.title: UK: Scottish islanders buy their remote home.
newsitem.headline: Scottish islanders buy their remote home.

text.p: Scottish islanders on Friday celebrated their success in buying their remote Hebridean home from its German owner and thanked wellwishers around the world who helped them do it.

A heritage trust set up by the islanders on Eigg, off the coast of Scotland, together with local bodies, has been trying for more than a year to buy their home from the latest in a string of absentee landlords.

German artist Marlin Eckhard Maruma last year rejected a bid from the islanders, who had launched an appeal for 800,000 pounds ($1.31 million). Maruma, who owned the island for just 18 months, asked instead for two million pounds.
But the sale went through after Hong Kong-based businessman Hans Rainer Erhardt called in a secured loan to Maruma's company, Eigg Islands Ltd, the trust said in a statement.
The trust said it raised 1.5 million pounds in its campaign to buy Eigg, which they will formally take over on June 12.
The 60 inhabitants of Eigg, mostly hardy crofters and fishermen, approached businesses, individuals, Britain's National Lottery and even used the internet to raise the money.
Maggie Fyffe, an islander and secretary of the Isle of Eigg Heritage Trust, said: "This is the day we have all dreamt about since we formed the partnership and set out into the unknown...
"We are all overjoyed at the outcome. The public's response has been absolutely fantastic."

Absentee landlords have been resented in the Scottish highlands ever since the 19th century "Clearances" in which whole villages were forced to emigrate when "lairds" decided arable land should be used as grazing for sheep.
